source.title: Quantization-Robust LLM Unlearning via Low-Rank Adaptation
source.citation: João Vitor Boer Abitante et al., 2026
source.authors: João Vitor Boer Abitante; Joana Meneguzzo Pasquali; Luan Fonseca Garcia; E. de Oliveira; Thomas da Silva Paula; Rodrigo C. Barros; L. Kupssinskü

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some table formatting is flattened, but the values can be assigned from the layout.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether 4-bit post-training quantization changes unlearning outcomes, and reports results that qualify the claim: most full-fine-tuning results do not show recovery, while LoRA results vary by dataset, method, and metric.
record.gate_note: The paper reports MUSE memorization, privacy-leakage, and utility metrics for full fine-tuning and LoRA unlearning before and after quantization. Its grid-search selections and theoretical discussion are not treated as results. The paper's cited findings from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: On Llama-2-7B with MUSE BOOKS/NEWS, the study measures whether 4-bit RTN quantization of unlearned weights restores forget-set memorization (Version D). It also tests its own LoRA method as a quantization-robust counter-method (Version F). Its own Table I shows no recovery toward the pre-unlearning model, which runs against D.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors claim Full-FT unlearning is masked by 4-bit PTQ and that merging LoRA adapters before PTQ preserves forgetting/privacy and reduces utility loss, with trade-offs depending on objective and dataset. However, their own Table I shows the 4-bit degradation in Full-FT is mainly in utility; forget-set metrics do not revert toward ftarget. The 'failure' claim leans on cited prior work [4] rather than on their own numbers.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GA or NPO with GDR/KLR, but constrains updates to LoRA adapters, merges them into the base weights, and then applies RTN PTQ. This is not a fine-tuning, activation-ablation, or prompting recovery attack.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary across BOOKS versus NEWS, GA/NPO objective and GDR/KLR regularizer; LoRA layer selection, rank, scaling, learning rate, duration, and regularization weight were grid-searched, but selected values are not reported here as outcomes.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network
record.problems: One model is tested (Llama-2-7B). No uncertainty estimates are reported. MUSE ROUGE-L memorization and utility scores are not chance-level targeted-knowledge accuracy. The study reports results for RTN PTQ; advanced quantization methods are discussed but not experimentally evaluated here.
record.rows_left_out: Table I 8-bit results, Table I PrivLeak and UtilityPres results, and Table II BF16-only comparisons were omitted to stay within 60 rows and prioritize forgetting measures under 4-bit quantization plus LoRA's 4-bit outcomes across all four reported metrics. The paper also discusses grid-search choices without reporting them as outcome rows.

untested.parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy versus chance (MUSE ROUGE-L only). Pre-unlearning comparison and utility rows are not recorded. No attacks other than PTQ.
Only RTN is tested. GPTQ/AWQ are mentioned from prior work but not run. Only Llama-2-7B and MUSE are used; no 8-bit rows.
LoRA is tested only against 4-bit RTN, not against relearning, activation ablation, or prompting attacks.

missing.what: ftarget (pre-unlearning) BF16/8-bit/4-bit rows: the correct comparator for whether 4-bit reverts to pre-unlearning behavior (e.g., BOOKS VerMem 4-bit 94.78, KnowMem 36.35)
Full-FT BF16 forgetting relative to ftarget (e.g., GA+GDR BOOKS KnowMem 36.30 vs 47.12), showing incomplete forgetting for regularized methods
Full-FT UtilityPres rows, including GA utility 0.00 and regularized-method drops at 4-bit (declared left out but needed for the A verdict)

record.verdict_notes: Version D state calls use the BF16-unlearned baseline as recorded. Quantization degrades all ROUGE scores, including the target model's, so the decisive comparison is against ftarget 4-bit, which also shows no recovery. LoRA rows were relinked to F only: their forget-metric states mean 'forgetting preserved', which would read as 'absent' under D. Single model, no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports forgetting and utility metrics, but does not report targeted-knowledge accuracy against a chance baseline. It tests quantization, not other simple attacks.
No relearning fine-tuning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocking access versus deletion is tested.
The study tests RTN 8-bit and 4-bit quantization, with reported results focused on BF16 versus 4-bit. It does not test other quantizers as an experiment.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context-information attack is tested.
LoRA is tested against 4-bit RTN quantization. The study does not test resistance to fine-tuning, activation edits, or prompting attacks.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The reported MUSE forgetting and utility metrics across BOOKS and NEWS
reader_labels.reason: The study reports forgetting scores and retain-set utility, but no chance-level accuracy reference; GA's authors-described near-complete forgetting coincides with UtilityPres 0.00 in Table I, while other methods show varied forgetting scores (r01-r24).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Full-FT methods after 4-bit RTN PTQ on BOOKS and NEWS
reader_labels.reason: For most method-dataset measures, quantization does not increase the reported forgetting metrics relative to BF16, and several decrease; only small increases occur in the listed NPO cases (r01-r24).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: LoRA unlearning followed by 4-bit RTN PTQ
reader_labels.reason: Most reported LoRA target-memory measures are stable or lower rather than showing knowledge recovery; some increase slightly, and outcomes vary across method and corpus (r25-r26, r29-r30, r33-r34, r37-r38, r41-r42, r45-r46, r49-r50, r53-r54).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LoRA on BOOKS, especially GA+GDR, NPO+GDR, and NPO+KLR
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports near-stable or improved forgetting metrics after 4-bit PTQ in these settings; NPO+GDR utility is also nearly stable, though utility and privacy outcomes are not uniformly preserved across all LoRA settings (r25-r28, r33-r40).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: LoRA on NEWS and BOOKS GA+KLR
reader_labels.reason: Outcomes differ by method and metric: NEWS utility declines under PTQ, and BOOKS GA+KLR utility and privacy leakage worsen relative to LoRA BF16 (r29, r31-r32, r41-r48, r51-r56).
